### 关于我们

#### 为什么做桥申

我是一名父亲，清华毕业。做桥申，起因是陪孩子准备去英国读书。

**看不清的路**

这条路上要准备的东西很多：A Level 课程要稳住，大学入学笔试要单独备考，竞赛要早做打算，面试要练习把思路讲出来，个人陈述要从自己的经历里一点点写出来。每一项都有自己的范围、时间节点和规则。真正让人费神的，往往不是哪一门有多难，而是信息不透明。哪些考试和目标专业有关，考纲到底覆盖什么、不覆盖什么，哪些说法有依据、哪些只是口口相传，常常要一遍遍回到官方渠道核对。资料越看越多，心里却不一定越踏实，因为很难分清哪一份还符合现在的规则。

**算不清的账**

准备的过程，也是一笔一笔的投入。课程、培训、备考材料，每一项单看都有道理，加在一起，就成了家里要认真盘算的事。很多家长都有过这样的犹豫：这个班报了，是不是真的用得上？不报，会不会恰好就差了这一点？钱花出去很快，花得值不值，却往往要过很久才看得清。

**放不下的心**

很多家长都会在孩子睡下以后，再打开电脑查一会儿资料，读几篇经验分享，对比几门课程，想弄明白下一步该往哪里走。怕选错方向，怕耽误孩子本来就紧张的时间，也怕自己做得还不够。这些担心很少说出口，但陪孩子走过这段路的家长，大多都懂。

**看不懂的题**

这一路走下来，有件事我想说实话：在学业上，我能给孩子的帮助其实很有限。孩子做的题，我这个老父亲早就看不懂了。想坐下来陪着一起琢磨，常常连题目在问什么都要想半天，更说不出哪一步错了。

一开始有些失落，后来也慢慢坦然了。遇到难题，孩子多半是自己查、自己推、自己改，错了再来一遍。我看在眼里，既骄傲，也心疼。骄傲的是，这一代孩子身上有一种很强的东西：一切靠自己。心疼的是，靠自己的路，往往也走得更孤单一些。

题目我帮不上，但我想，孩子靠自己的时候，至少应该有个地方，能自己练，自己发现问题。

**所以我们做了桥申**

我们想把这段路上需要下真功夫的部分，整理成学生可以自己练的内容，也想对这几种心情给出实在的回应：

- **对信息不透明**：每门训练先写明练什么、不练什么。训练题是原创的，就直接说是原创，不装成官方试卷。
- **对经济压力**：考季卡 3 个月 ¥399，希望这个价格是普通家庭能负担的。【请 Jose 确认措辞】
- **对放不下的心**：孩子可以自己练，每次练习都有记录和反馈，能看到自己哪里在进步、哪里还要再想一想。

也想坦白说一句：桥申解决不了所有问题。它能做的，是让孩子用更低的成本多练一些，更早发现自己卡在哪里。至于要不要上培训班，还是要看每个孩子的情况，桥申并不是要替代所有课程。

申请准备没有捷径，但每一步都可以有更清楚的依据。

—— 桥申团队

#### 桥申做什么

- **A Level**：目前只做 CAIE 9709 Pure 3。
- **竞赛**：BMO、BPhO 题库，以及竞赛规划。
- **大学入学考试**：以 TMUA、STEP、TARA 为主；ESAT、UCAT、CSAT、IELTS、LNAT 也有部分训练内容；MAT、PAT 只作历史训练。
- **面试**：覆盖理工、社会科学、人文、剑桥学院评估、香港院校面试和雅思口语等方向，练习说清假设、解释方法、回应追问。
- **文书**：支持 UCAS 个人陈述三问和香港院校单篇文书，从学生自己的真实经历出发整理和修改。

#### 我们坚持什么

- 不代写文书，不编造经历。文书必须由学生本人完成。
- 不押题。训练题都是原创，用来练能力，不预测考试内容。
- 不承诺提分、录取、获奖或面试通过。
- AI 反馈只用于训练复盘，可能出错，不是人工或官方批改。
- 我们与任何大学或考试机构都没有官方合作；院校和考试要求以官方发布为准。

#### 联系我们

桥申还在持续改进和完善中。如果你在使用时发现问题，或者有任何建议，欢迎写信告诉我们，我们会认真对待每一条意见。

桥申团队：hello@drforest.ai

### About QiaoShen

#### Why we built QiaoShen

I'm a father and a Tsinghua graduate. QiaoShen began with helping my child prepare to study in the UK.

**A road that's hard to see clearly**

That preparation has a lot of moving parts. A Level grades need to hold steady. University admissions tests need their own preparation. Competitions take planning well in advance. Interviews mean learning to think out loud. And a personal statement has to be written, slowly, from your own experience. Each comes with its own syllabus, deadlines and rules.

What wore on us most wasn't that any single part was especially hard. It was how unclear the information often was. Which tests matter for which courses? What does a syllabus actually cover, and what does it leave out? Which advice rests on official guidance, and which is simply passed from one family to the next? We kept going back to the official sources to check. The more we read, the less sure we sometimes felt, because it was hard to tell which material still reflected the current rules.

**Costs that add up**

Preparation is also an investment, made one decision at a time. Classes, training courses, revision materials: each makes sense on its own, but together they become something a family has to think through carefully. Many parents know the question well. Will this course really help? And if we skip it, will that turn out to be the one thing that was missing? Spending happens quickly. Knowing whether it was worth it often takes much longer.

**Worries that are hard to put down**

Many parents find themselves back at the computer after their child has gone to bed, reading one more guide, comparing one more course, trying to work out what comes next. We worry about choosing the wrong direction, about using up time our children don't have to spare, and about not doing enough ourselves. These worries are rarely said out loud, but most parents who have walked this road with a child will recognise them.

**Problems I can no longer follow**

If I'm honest, I have been able to help my child with their studies far less than I expected. Somewhere along the way, I stopped being able to follow the problems they were working on. When I sat down to look, it often took me a while just to understand what a question was asking, let alone spot where a step had gone wrong.

At first that felt like a loss. Over time I made peace with it. When my child got stuck, they worked it out themselves: looking things up, reasoning it through, trying again after each mistake. Watching that, I feel proud, and my heart aches a little too. Proud, because this generation has something genuinely strong in them: they rely on themselves. And it aches, because relying on yourself can be a lonely road.

I can't help with the problems. But I believe that when children are relying on themselves, they should at least have somewhere to practise on their own and find their own gaps.

**So we built QiaoShen**

We wanted to turn the parts of this journey that need real, steady work into something students can practise on their own, and to answer each of those feelings in a practical way:

- **For unclear information**: every area states plainly what it covers and what it doesn't. Our practice questions are original, and we say so rather than presenting them as official papers.
- **For the cost**: the Exam Season Pass is ¥399 for 3 months — a price we hope ordinary families can afford. [Jose to confirm wording]
- **For the worry**: students can practise on their own, with a record of their work and feedback on each attempt, so they can see where they are improving and what still needs another look.

We also want to be honest: QiaoShen can't solve everything. What it can do is give students more practice at a lower cost and help them spot where they get stuck earlier. Whether to take a class still depends on each student, and QiaoShen isn't meant to replace every course.

There are no shortcuts in preparing an application, but every step can rest on clearer ground.

— The QiaoShen team

#### What QiaoShen offers

- **A Level**: CAIE 9709 Pure 3 only, for now.
- **Competitions**: BMO and BPhO question banks, plus competition planning.
- **University admissions tests**: a focus on TMUA, STEP and TARA, with some practice material for ESAT, UCAT, CSAT, IELTS and LNAT. MAT and PAT are kept for historical practice only.
- **Interviews**: practice across STEM, social sciences, humanities, Cambridge college assessments, Hong Kong university interviews and IELTS Speaking, focused on stating assumptions, explaining your method and handling follow-up questions.
- **Personal statements**: support for the three UCAS questions and single-essay statements for Hong Kong universities, built from the student's own experience.

#### What we stand by

- We don't write personal statements for students or invent experiences. Every statement must be the student's own work.
- We don't try to predict exam questions. Our practice questions are original and built to develop skills.
- We don't promise higher scores, offers, awards or interview success.
- AI feedback is for practice and review only. It can be wrong, and it is not marking by a teacher or an exam board.
- We have no official partnership with any university or exam board. Always check requirements with the official sources.

#### Contact

QiaoShen is still being improved. If you notice a problem or have a suggestion, we'd really like to hear from you, and we take every piece of feedback seriously.

The QiaoShen team: hello@drforest.ai
